question: Calculate: \(25\times4+25\times6=?\)
solution: \(25\times4=100\) and \(25\times6=150\). Adding them gives 250. You can also first calculate \(25\times(4+6)\).

edges.reason: Two-digit mental addition supports some final addition steps. A small-digit sum, decomposed computation or written algorithm also evaluates a two-step expression; Gemini incorrectly requires a specific oral procedure.
Multiplication-before-addition is an expression convention. A learner may evaluate needed products by grouping or counting without memorizing the earlier table, so preparation is appropriate.
Column addition reinforces place-value alignment and regrouping. Mental hundreds/tens sums can be obtained by decomposition and unit counts without laying out written columns.
Mental arithmetic on hundreds and tens uses the values of those places in three-digit numbers.

Written addition prepares vertical alignment and repeated carrying. In multiplication the carried amount is added to one digit product, so the full three-digit column-addition procedure is not executed.

The general digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm contains digit products with seven, eight and nine. Their values are required, without demanding rote recitation as the exclusive way to obtain them.

Two-digit division broadens which expression steps can be computed. The precedence convention and a three-step calculation can also be practiced with one-digit divisors; the wider algorithm is preparation.
